Japan’s FM urges Russia to release journalist detained on Sakhalin
According to Ukrinform, this was reported by Kyodo News, citing a statement from Japan’s Foreign Ministry.
Motegi and Lavrov met on the sidelines of a G20 foreign ministers’ meeting that began the same day in the U.S. state of Georgia.
Tensions between the two countries escalated further in early October when a Japanese journalist was detained on Sakhalin on suspicion of espionage.
Japan’s Foreign Ministry said Motegi and Lavrov had agreed to maintain communication despite strained relations.
In addition, Japan’s foreign minister urged Russia to take steps toward achieving a just and lasting peace in connection with its full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
Motegi also clearly outlined Japan’s position on unresolved bilateral issues, including those concerning islands off the coast of Hokkaido that are under Russian control.
Meanwhile, Russia’s Foreign Ministry said Lavrov had stressed during the meeting that Japan must abandon its “unfriendly policy” toward Russia if it wanted to restore full-fledged dialogue. The ministry added that Friday’s meeting had taken place at Japan’s request.
The first official meeting between the Japanese and Russian foreign ministers in about five years took place amid deteriorating bilateral relations following the sanctions imposed on Russia by Japan and other G7 members over Moscow’s war against Ukraine. The last official meeting between the two countries’ foreign ministers was held in September 2021.
As Ukrinform reported, Yuki Imai, a journalist with Japan’s Hokkaido Shimbun newspaper, was detained in Russia’s Sakhalin region shortly before his scheduled departure from Russia. Moscow’s Lefortovo District Court ordered his detention for two months, until December 12.
Russia’s Federal Security Service (FSB) claimed that the journalist had allegedly collected information about Russia’s defense capabilities “in the interests of one of Japan’s intelligence services.”
Japan’s Foreign Ministry summoned the Russian ambassador and lodged a protest over the detention of a Japanese citizen without prior explanation to the Japanese government.
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi rejected Russia’s espionage allegations against the Japanese journalist detained by Moscow.

articles.title: ‘We won't transport weapons’: Dockworkers at over 100 ports strike over Israel
articles.body:
Dockworkers in several European countries and on other continents went on strike Friday, with one of their main demands being an end to weapons shipments to Israel through their ports. 
Dockworkers' unions in France, Italy, Spain, Greece, Turkey and Morocco issued a joint call opposing arms shipments and demanding an end to what they described as "the militarization of ports." They also called for an end to the war in Gaza.
The joint statement also declared: "Ports must not be used to transport weapons, ammunition, military equipment or troops. Dockworkers do not work for war!" According to the unions, more than 100 ports in several countries joined the protest, and the actions could disrupt maritime traffic in Europe, the Mediterranean region and North America. During the demonstrations, workers also raised demands concerning social rights, but the main focus was stopping the movement of weapons through ports. Palestinian flags could be seen in some of the photographs circulated from the protests.
In Greece, dockworkers' unions declared a strike at Piraeus, the country's largest port. Giorgos Gogos, president of the local dockworkers' union, said: "We do not want to take part in any war, anywhere in the world. We do not want our ports to serve as transit hubs for military equipment intended to kill people."
In Turkey, protesters gathered outside Haydarpasa port in Istanbul, carrying a banner reading: "No to war, no to armament!" In Italy, demonstrations were planned at major ports, including Genoa, Trieste and Gioia Tauro.
Meanwhile, the French dockworkers' union called a one-day strike at major ports, including Le Havre, Marseille, Dunkirk and Rouen. The union said it opposed what it described as "the militarization of port facilities." Earlier this month, pro-Palestinian workers at an airport in France attempted to prevent a shipment intended for Israeli defense company Elbit from being flown out.
Despite the large number of ports involved in Friday's protests, experts estimated that the impact on maritime operations would be limited. Marcus Baker, global head of marine, cargo and logistics at insurance and risk advisory firm Marsh, told the Associated Press that the one-day strike was unlikely to significantly disrupt global trade, although it could affect perishable goods and time-sensitive shipments. 
He said Friday's strike and similar actions would further complicate supply chains already under pressure from tensions in the Middle East, climate-related events such as El Niño storms, restrictions affecting the Rhine River and Panama Canal, and changes in tariffs imposed by various countries.
Since the beginning of the Swords of Iron war, several countries have imposed restrictions on the transit of weapons bound for Israel through their territory. Spain, for example, announced an official policy barring ships carrying weapons for Israel from docking at its ports. 
The first measure of this kind was implemented in 2024, when Madrid refused to allow the Marianne Danica, a vessel arriving from India carrying dozens of tons of explosives, to dock at the port of Cartagena. Other vessels were subsequently denied permission to dock, including ships from the United States suspected of transporting weapons to Israel.
In March, U.S. President Donald Trump said France had barred American aircraft carrying supplies for Israel from passing through its territory, against the backdrop of French opposition to Israeli military operations in Gaza and Lebanon.

articles.title: US approves $2.1 billion Patriot missile sale to Ukraine
articles.body:
Breadcrumb
US approves $2.1 billion Patriot missile sale to Ukraine
The US State Department said on Friday it had approved the sale of 500 Patriot PAC-3 missiles to Ukraine for an estimated $2.1 billion.
Ukraine will pay for the defensive interceptor missiles with contributions from Canada, Germany and Norway routed through the US JUMPSTART programme, along with national funds financed by the European Union's Ukraine Support Loan, the State Department said in a statement.
Delayed missile deliveries added to Ukraine's tensions with the US after President Donald Trump announced a diesel deal with Russia and criticised Zelensky for Ukraine's unwillingness to stop attacks on Russian refineries.
President Volodymyr Zelensky said earlier this week that Ukraine had been waiting for almost a month for the US to sign off on critical missile supplies, as Russia stepped up attacks on energy and civilian infrastructure.
The Ukrainian leader has repeatedly called on the US, which supplies missiles purchased by NATO allies under a programme known as PURL, to speed up deliveries ahead of winter.
Lockheed Martin is the principal contractor for the sale.
The US has supplied large quantities of weapons to allies while also using munitions in its own military operations in Iran, raising concerns about inventories of key air defence and precision-guided weapons.
In July, the US Army awarded Lockheed a contract worth up to $58.6 billion to produce Patriot interceptor missiles.
Lockheed has said that deal would allow it to follow through on a promise to triple PAC-3 MSE production capacity by the end of 2030 and increase jobs at its Camden, Arkansas, plant by 50%, to about 1,850 from 1,200. Lockheed previously announced Patriot PAC-3 missile interceptor production would go to 2,000 units annually.
Pentagon negotiators are pressing contractors to move much faster, with tentative production agreements struck earlier this year at the centre of efforts to increase missile output.

articles.title: Ukraine hopes European partners will help fund purchase of 500 Patriot missiles – Zelensky
articles.body:
Ukraine hopes European partners will help fund purchase of 500 Patriot missiles – Zelensky
According to an Ukrinform correspondent, the head of state made the remarks while speaking to the media in Turkey, commenting on the U.S. approval of the sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine and the prospects for missile deliveries this winter.
"We have an understanding of what we will have this winter. It is not enough. It is not enough to protect [us]... 500 missiles... We are grateful to the United States. This is a very good offer. Of course, we need to raise funds for this offer. I am confident that we will find the funding with the help of our partners, primarily European ones," he said.
Zelensky noted that deliveries of the missiles had been postponed by several years, partly due to the specifics of their production. At the same time, he said the United States was supplying, or was ready to supply, weapons from its stockpiles to Ukraine only slowly, and that this pace was insufficient to ensure adequate protection for Ukrainians. He also cited the conflict in the Middle East as another challenge affecting the allocation of all aid packages.
He noted that Ukraine continued its work on a bilateral track with Europe and other countries.
"If we were to rely only on the number coming from the United States, it would be... things are already painful for us, and they would be even more painful," he said.
At the same time, Zelensky stressed that the U.S. package remained very important.
"Several times during this war, we have done this... and in various discussions, this arrangement of swapping places in the queue has worked. I will try to do this with some partners. With that package of 500 [missiles], we could get 10, 20 or 30 [missiles] from someone else, sign the relevant guarantees and agreements that we would later replenish those supplies from the U.S. package, with some interest or perhaps without interest. So this is a major ongoing daily effort," he said.
As Ukrinform reported, the U.S. Department of State approved the possible sale to Ukraine of 500 PAC-3 MSE missiles for Patriot air defense systems, worth a total of $2.1 billion.

articles.title: Iran says no plans to meet U.S. officials, consultations with mediators continue
articles.body:
DOHA, Oct. 31 (Xinhua) -- Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi said that Tehran currently has no plans to meet with U.S. officials, while consultations with Qatari and Pakistani mediators continue over Iran's conditions for resolving the crisis, Qatar's Al Jazeera reported Saturday.
In an interview with Al Jazeera, Araghchi dismissed reports of possible meetings as media speculation, saying Iran saw no need to meet with American officials at present.
He said Tehran would decide whether to hold direct or indirect negotiations after Washington accepted Iran's conditions.
Araghchi said an Iranian delegation had traveled to Qatar for further discussions, adding that his aide was there to continue consultations with mediators.
According to Araghchi, Iran's conditions include recognition of a new shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz that Tehran had worked out with Oman, and the closure of other routes.
He said Tehran also sought the lifting of sanctions imposed after the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding (MoU), a reduction in U.S. military forces in the region, the restoration of sanctions waivers for Iranian oil exports, and the release of all frozen Iranian funds, including those held in Qatar.
Iran also demanded an end to hostilities on all fronts, including Lebanon, he said.
Araghchi said mediators had presented proposals concerning Iran's nuclear program, which Tehran was reviewing as part of what he described as a second phase.
The Iranian foreign minister also said a letter from U.S. Vice President JD Vance had been reviewed at high-level meetings, describing the American effort to open the door to broader dialogue and understanding as a "positive step."
On Feb. 28, Israel and the United States launched joint attacks on Tehran and other Iranian cities. Iran responded with waves of missile and drone attacks targeting Israel and U.S. bases and assets in the region, and tightened its grip on the Strait of Hormuz.
A ceasefire was achieved between the warring parties on April 8. On June 18, Iran and the United States signed the MoU on ending the war in the region on all fronts.
Under the MoU, the two countries were scheduled to hold negotiations within 60 days, ending on Aug. 17, to reach a final agreement on Iran's nuclear program and the removal of sanctions. However, they failed to make sufficient progress toward a deal. ■

articles.title: Iran targeted USS Abraham Lincoln with cruise missile, Navy Cmdr. says
articles.body:
Iran targeted USS Abraham Lincoln with cruise missile, Navy Cmdr. says
TEHRAN - Iran's Navy targeted the USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier with a strategic cruise missile during the 40-day Ramadan War, the Iranian Navy's deputy coordinator has said, noting that the force carried out more than 20 operations against U.S. warships and around 300 operations against American interests in various locations.
Rear Admiral Jalil Moghadam said Iranian forces identified the carrier during the first two days of the conflict, using visual observation and available surveillance systems to track its position.
Speaking to the IRNA news agency, Moghadam said the Navy launched the missile after locating the carrier. He added that the vessel halted flight operations for three days following the strike before moving farther away from Iran's coastline.
According to the official, Iranian naval forces concluded that the carrier had been hit after examining a series of developments following the operation.
Moghadam said aircraft operating from the carrier attacked Iran's second and third naval regions on the third day of the war. He noted that the carrier conducted no launches or flights for three days after Iran's operation.
He added that, on the day of the attack or that night, the carrier requested assistance from a coastal country and reported having injured personnel.
"Later, it was announced that the carrier had caught fire," Moghadam said, adding that images released from the site of the damage did not, in his assessment, correspond to an ordinary fire.
He said the images showed ruptures in the hull and deformation of the structure, which he interpreted as evidence of a missile strike.
 
Iran Navy rejects claims of destruction
Moghadam also rejected U.S. claims that Iran's naval forces had been destroyed, arguing that developments during and after the war demonstrated that the force remained operational.
He said U.S. and Israeli forces had refrained from approaching Iran's coastline, particularly the Strait of Hormuz, and questioned why they had remained hundreds of kilometers away if Iran's naval capabilities had been eliminated.
The official mentioned that Iranian naval forces had continued to inflict damage on U.S. and Israeli interests during the 40-day conflict and after the ceasefire.
He added that the Navy had reviewed its military doctrine following the conflict, incorporating lessons from the war and reassessing its equipment and operational priorities.
Moghadam said that, in the event of another war, Iran's naval operations would extend beyond the scope of the previous conflict, citing improvements in the force's equipment and capabilities.
He also described the Strait of Hormuz as a strategic advantage for Iran, arguing that regional maritime security would not return to its desired state while U.S. forces remained in the region.
The Iranian Navy official's remarks come amid continued tensions between Tehran and Washington over regional security and the strategic waterway, through which a significant share of global oil shipments passes.

articles.title: Iran’s nuclear doctrine debate reflects national demand for stronger deterrence
articles.body:
Iran’s nuclear doctrine debate reflects national demand for stronger deterrence
TEHRAN — Tehran’s interim Friday prayer leader, Mohammad Javad Haj Ali Akbari, has described calls to review Iran’s nuclear doctrine as a growing national demand rooted in the Iranian people’s experience of Western conduct, heightened security concerns and the need to strengthen the country’s deterrence capabilities.
Addressing worshippers during Friday prayers in the Iranian capital on October 30, Haj Ali Akbari said the debate over a possible revision of the country’s nuclear doctrine should not be dismissed as an emotional reaction or attributed to a particular political faction. Rather, he argued, it reflects a broader public reassessment of the security requirements facing Iran following years of confrontation, unfulfilled commitments and hostile actions by its adversaries.
His remarks come amid renewed public discussion in Iran about the country’s nuclear policy and the relationship between its established positions, national security requirements and the evolving regional and international environment.
A debate shaped by security concerns
Haj Ali Akbari said Iran’s adversaries had crossed the nation’s red lines, pointing to the assassination of the martyred Leader of the Islamic Revolution, Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei, and 'repeated failures' to honor commitments and agreements.
He argued that the Iranian people’s accumulated experience had prompted a more considered debate about the country’s deterrence requirements, including whether its nuclear doctrine should be reviewed in light of the security challenges it faces.
According to the cleric, the proposal is rooted in the Iranian nation’s right to live in dignity and security. He stressed that the discussion should be understood as a matter of national concern rather than an initiative belonging to any single political group or current.
Haj Ali Akbari also said that some people had reacted angrily to the proposal but maintained that the public discussion surrounding it reflected a broader demand that policymakers should examine seriously.
Citing previous surveys, he said more than 70 percent of respondents in some polls had supported reviewing Iran’s nuclear doctrine.
He added that calls for reconsideration had subsequently emerged from a range of social and professional groups, including university students, school students, academics, intellectuals and professional associations.
The cleric urged universities, researchers, security specialists and other experts to contribute to the debate by conducting substantive studies and developing policy proposals. He also called on the relevant authorities to undertake further assessments, with the aim of submitting the resulting recommendations to the Leader of the Islamic Revolution, Ayatollah Seyyed Mojtaba Hosseini Khamenei.
He emphasized that the final decision rested with the Leader and said that any decision he made would be followed.
Negotiations and the question of vigilance
Alongside the nuclear doctrine debate, Haj Ali Akbari cautioned against interpreting US calls for negotiations, diplomatic correspondence, or the involvement of intermediaries as grounds for relaxing Iran’s vigilance.
Drawing on Iran’s experience of dealings with Washington, he argued that diplomatic overtures should be assessed in the context of the other side’s conduct and actions, rather than its statements alone.
He warned that, in some circumstances, US messages and proposals for negotiations could coincide with more serious threats than those conveyed through explicit declarations of hostility. His remarks underscored the importance of maintaining vigilance while assessing diplomatic initiatives.
The comments reflect a central concern in Iranian political and security discourse: that diplomatic engagement must be evaluated alongside practical guarantees, respect for commitments, and the broader security environment.
For Tehran, the question is not simply whether negotiations are proposed, but whether the process can produce credible and lasting commitments while safeguarding Iran’s national interests.
From public debate to policy assessment
Haj Ali Akbari’s remarks place the nuclear doctrine debate within a wider discussion about deterrence, national sovereignty and the country's response to changing security conditions.
 
By calling for contributions from universities, professional bodies and relevant specialists, he presented the issue as one requiring sustained examination rather than a decision driven by immediate political pressures.
The distinction is significant: a public demand for a review does not, in itself, constitute a formal change in national policy. Any revision would require consideration by the competent authorities and a decision through the country's established institutional framework.
Iran's nuclear policy has long been a subject of international debate, particularly in relation to its stated position against nuclear weapons, its nuclear program and the country's security concerns. A discussion about revising the doctrine therefore raises questions that extend beyond technical nuclear policy to include deterrence, strategic calculations and the country's assessment of the international environment.
Haj Ali Akbari called for the debate to be informed by expert analysis and national considerations, while reaffirming that the Leader would make the final decision.
His remarks signal that calls for a reassessment of Iran's nuclear doctrine have become an issue of public and political discussion, with supporters framing the debate around national security, deterrence and the lessons drawn from past confrontations. Whether that discussion results in any change in policy remains a matter for the country's competent decision-making authorities.

articles.title: US oil companies tripled profits during Iran war – NYT
articles.body:
US oil companies tripled profits during Iran war – NYT
The US’ largest oil companies almost tripled their profits during the US-Israeli war on Iran, the New York Times has reported, at a time when soaring energy costs threaten to wipe out US President Donald Trump’s Republican Party in the upcoming midterm elections.
The American oil giants – including Chevron, Exxon Mobil, and Valero – earned $130 billion in profits between April and September, according to six months worth of financial results covering more than 50 companies, combined by the New York Times. In the same period last year, these companies made less than $47 billion.
This windfall is an almost direct mirror of the extra $147 billion Americans spent on gasoline and diesel since American and Israeli warplanes began striking Iran on February 28.
With the Strait of Hormuz closed to shipping for almost all of the last six months, and Yemen’s Houthis attacking Saudi extraction sites and shipping in the Red Sea, American producers have reaped the benefit of high oil prices, with Chevron and Exxon Mobil recording higher profits than at any point since the Ukraine conflict escalated in 2022.
Exxon’s third-quarter profit more than doubled this year, while Chevron’s almost tripled.
American refiners have taken advantage of the widespread destruction of refining sites in the Gulf region, and the threat of Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian refineries, leveraging their safe location inside the US. Valero and Phillips 66 both posted all-time record third-quarter profits this year.
Europe’s oil giants have posted similar results, with Shell, TotalEnergies, and Repsol all more than doubling their earnings last quarter over the same timeframe in 2025, as Europeans grapple with record energy bills. Some European finance ministers have demanded that the EU impose windfall taxes on these companies in response.
At $4.29 per gallon as of Monday, US gasoline prices are now higher than they were at any point during former President Joe Biden’s four years in office, with the exception of the first three months after the escalation of the Ukraine conflict. Trump has described the elevated prices as a “small price to pay for” preventing Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon, but voters aren’t convinced.
This week, 72% of respondents told a Gallup poll that gasoline prices are “extremely” important in how they plan to vote in next week’s midterm elections. Most polling organizations show the Republican Party on track to lose one or both houses of Congress next week, with the GOP trailing the Democrats by between eight and nine points nationwide.
Trump has tried to alleviate some of this damage by lifting sanctions on Russian diesel, and at least three diesel tankers have left Russian ports en route to the US. Trump has also pressed Ukrainian leader Vladimir Zelensky to cease attacks on Russian refineries, but Zelensky has apparently ignored these requests.

articles.title: Iranian delegation arrives in Qatar for talks: Report

The sources said the US delegation could hold direct talks with Iranian negotiators in the Qatari capital.

articles.title: Ukrainian forces strike rocket fuel plant in Russia's Rostov region
articles.body:
Ukrainian forces strike rocket fuel plant in Russia's Rostov region
According to Ukrinform, the General Staff of the Ukrainian Armed Forces reported this on Telegram.
On the night of October 30-31, units of Ukraine's Defense Forces struck the Kamensky Combine, a Russian military-industrial complex facility in the town of Kamensk-Shakhtinsky in the Rostov region.
The attack involved a combination of weapons – strike drones and missile forces, including Neptune coastal missile systems operated by the Ukrainian Navy.
A fire at a finished products warehouse has been confirmed. Four production workshops were also damaged.
The Kamensky Combine manufactures solid rocket fuel for Uragan, Smerch and Tornado-S multiple launch rocket systems, as well as for a number of missile systems and air-launched weapons.
Four warehouses storing military supplies for the Russian army were also hit – near Khartsyzk and Dokuchaievsk in the Donetsk region, Novovasylivka in the Zaporizhzhia region, and Novoaidar in the Luhansk region.

articles.title: Trump admin approves potential Patriot missiles sale to Ukraine
articles.body:
Trump admin approves potential Patriot missiles sale to Ukraine
The Trump administration on Friday green-lit the sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine, the State Department said, but the Ukrainian president warned deliveries could take years.
The approval, which goes to Congress for review, comes after weeks of complaints by Ukrainian authorities that its supplies of the interceptor missiles were dwindling.
"The proposed sale will improve Ukraine's capability to meet current and future threats by improving its integrated air and missile defense capabilities," the department said in a statement.
The statement did not provide an estimate for when the weapons could be delivered to Ukraine.
But Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said late Friday in a post on X that "deliveries may begin ONLY IN A FEW YEARS."
"We are asking our American partners to find a solution for the time when there is a real danger and a real need to use PAC-3 interceptors," Zelensky said, using an acronym for the weapons.
The Ukrainian leader suggested that the US and European allies could give his country missiles they have stockpiled now, which would later be replenished by this new purchase.
Patriot missiles are among the most important weapons Ukraine has to intercept Russian drones and missiles.
"This proposed sale will support the foreign policy and national security objectives of the United States by improving the security of a partner country that is a force for political and economic stability in Europe," the State Department said.
US-Ukraine tensions spiked earlier this month after Washington struck a diesel fuel deal with Russia. Ukraine also said that the US was slowing its access to satellite internet services and had stopped some intelligence sharing.
Tensions eased after Zelensky held talks with US envoys in Oslo on October 20.
The State Department said the weapons sale would be paid for with by donations from Ukraine's allies but not with US funds.
(FRANCE 24 with AFP)

articles.title: 'A lot of lies': Kaja Kallas criticises Russian FM Lavrov following G20 meetings
articles.body:
British Foreign Minister Ed Miliband said he had told Lavrov in the plenary that "he should have the courage to tell Putin that Russia will not win this war."
European Union foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas accused Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov of telling "a lot of lies" on topics such as the Ukraine war during talks with G20 ministers in Atlanta on Friday.
"We were talking about the big geopolitical crisis, including Ukraine, and we were able to address Sergey Lavrov head on with this," she told the AFP news agency.
"Of course, he put forward a lot of lies, a lot of false narratives" that Europeans challenged, Kallas added.
European officials also reportedly used the opportunity to put further pressure on Moscow as they sought to secure a ceasefire in the Black Sea - prompting pushback from Lavrov, a diplomatic source told AFP.
British Foreign Minister Ed Miliband said he had also told Lavrov in the plenary that "he should have the courage to tell Putin that Russia will not win this war."
The UK minister is also said to have confronted Lavrov over a recent attack on a Dnipro railway that killed 15 people as he stressed Moscow was the "aggressor" in the conflict, which began in February 2022 when Russian forces launched their full-scale invasion.
In a press conference on Friday, Lavrov "welcomed" the US' willingness to engage in dialogue with Moscow while hitting out at what he called Europe's "arrogant boycott."
"This is a good lesson for our European colleagues," he said of Washington's approach.
Several officials at the meetings also reportedly refused to stand for a "family photo" with Lavrov, leading US organisers to cancel the picture.
The G20 meetings come just days before the US' key midterm elections, which will determine the balance of power in Congress for President Donald Trump's final two years in office.
US approves Patriots package for Ukraine
On Friday, the US State Department announced that Washington had green-lit a package of 500 Patriot PAC-3 interceptors worth $2.1 billion for Ukraine.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has continued to plead with US and European allies for more interceptors for its forces as Ukraine continues to weather Russian missile and drone attacks.
And while he welcomed the new package and thanked the US for its "strong decision," he warned that delivery could take years.
"Five hundred PAC-3 interceptors is a substantial number, and very soon – this winter – they COULD make for a highly effective defence package," Zelenskyy wrote in a post on X.
"However, it has been stipulated that deliveries may begin ONLY IN A FEW YEARS," he added. "We are asking our American partners to find a solution for the time when there is a real danger and a real need to use PAC-3 interceptors."
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio met with Lavrov on the sidelines of the G20 in Atlanta.

articles.title: US orders non-emergency personnel to leave Saudi Arabia amid Houthi attacks
articles.body:
The US State Department has ordered non-emergency government employees and their families to leave Saudi Arabia amid escalating attacks by Yemen’s Houthi group, the US Embassy said Friday, Anadolu reports.
In a security alert, the US Mission to Saudi Arabia said the departure order took effect on Oct. 23 due to safety risks.
The mission warned that Houthi attacks on civilian airports and critical infrastructure had caused casualties and major travel disruptions, adding that hostilities could escalate rapidly.
US government employees must obtain special authorization to use airports in Saudi Arabia following recent missile and drone attacks, the statement said.
The embassy said Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport had partially reopened, while airports in Jeddah and Dammam remained operational with some delays and cancellations.
It also urged US citizens to exercise extreme caution when traveling by air and warned against photographing missile interceptions or attack sites, citing Saudi regulations.
The alert comes amid intensified Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia.
On Thursday, the Saudi-led coalition announced that its air defenses had intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles launched by the Houthis toward Riyadh.
On Friday, the coalition reported intercepting a Houthi cruise missile targeting western Saudi Arabia, as well as a drone in the Riyadh region.
The Houthis have also claimed attacks on Saudi oil facilities and airports in recent days.
The Saudi-led coalition intervened in Yemen in March 2015 to support the internationally recognized government against the Houthis, who have controlled the capital Sanaa since September 2014.

articles.title: G20 drops group photo as Europeans refuse to stand with Lavrov
articles.body:
G20 drops group photo as Europeans refuse to stand with Lavrov
The United States has scrapped a traditional group photo of foreign ministers after European officials refused to be pictured alongside Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov.
The move exposes deep rifts at the heart of the Group of 20 (G20), whose foreign ministers are meeting in the southern city of Atlanta in the United States for talks overshadowed by the wars in Ukraine and Iran.
“There will be no family photo featuring our European partners together with Mr Lavrov,” German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said, according to the dpa news agency.
Lavrov, who remains under Western sanctions imposed after Russia’s 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine, arrived in Atlanta ahead of the talks, Russian state media reported. Moscow said on Thursday that he would use his speech to argue against international sanctions. Ukraine was not invited, the Abu Dhabi-based newspaper The National reported.
A diplomatic source told the AFP news agency that Russia’s presence at the G20 “in no way legitimises its actions”.
The European Union’s foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas pledged on Thursday to urge G20 partners to strengthen support for Ukraine and pursue accountability through a special tribunal and claims commission, after a Russian strike on a Ukrainian railway station killed at least 14 people earlier that day.
The meeting also comes weeks after US President Donald Trump issued sanctions waivers allowing Russia to export diesel to ease fuel prices before the November 3 midterm elections.
Opening the talks, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio urged members to cooperate on economic and geopolitical crises threatening global trade, energy and food supplies, and freedom of navigation, dpa reported. Iran blocked the Strait of Hormuz after US-Israeli strikes began in late February, and global energy prices have risen sharply since.
“Both maritime and food security drive economic security,” Rubio wrote on X.
No joint statement is expected. A diplomatic source told the AFP news agency that Washington will instead publish a chair’s summary it has drafted. The source added: “The G20 is no longer really a forum where foreign ministers can reach agreement on a statement.”
No government has said whether Rubio and Lavrov will hold a formal bilateral meeting.
China sent Executive Vice Foreign Minister Ma Zhaoxu in place of Foreign Minister Wang Yi, according to a delegation list released by the Department of State. South Africa, a founding G20 member, has been excluded by Washington, and the African Union is represented by Burundi’s Edouard Bizimana.
The Atlanta talks are the last ministerial meeting of the US G20 presidency before leaders meet in Miami on December 14 and 15.

articles.title: Two civilians killed in Ukrainian strike on Russia – governor
articles.body:
Two civilians killed in Ukrainian strike on Russia – governor
Two people have been killed and five others wounded in Ukrainian drone attacks on Bryansk Region, western Russia, local governor Egor Kovalchuk has said.
A 30-year-old woman and a 41-year-old man lost their lives after a kamikaze-drone struck a private home in the settlement of Klimovo, not far from Russia’s border with Ukraine, Kovalchuk wrote in a post on Max on Saturday.
“A tragedy in the border area – civilians killed,” he said, expressing condolences to the relatives of the victims.
Four females and one male were injured by Kiev’s UAVs elsewhere in the region, including a 73-year-old woman in the village of Pogar and a 19-year-old boy in Voronok, he added.
Earlier in the day, Belgorod Region Governor Aleksandr Shuvayev said that he had received information from emergency services about a civilian being killed in a Ukrainian drone attack in Schebekino District. The exact time it happened is not yet known, he added.
Four people were also wounded in Ukrainian UAV and artillery strikes across the region over the past 24 hours, Shuvayev said. Three of them are still hospitalized, according to the governor.
Kursk Region has also been extensively targeted by Ukrainian forces, with one man wounded in the village of Chernitsyno and another one in Lgov, Kursk Governor Aleksandr Khinshtein has said.
Bryansk, Belgorod, and Kursk regions, which all border Ukraine, have come under regular attacks since the escalation between Moscow and Kiev in February 2022.
The Russian Defense Ministry said on Saturday morning that a total of 433 fixed-wing Ukrainian drones were destroyed by air defenses in 19 Russian regions overnight.
Moscow has accused Ukraine of deliberately targeting residential areas and civilian infrastructure to compensate for setbacks on the battlefield where Russian forces continue to advance.
In response to Ukrainian terrorist attacks, Russia has intensified its long-range missile and drone campaign against Ukraine’s military facilities and infrastructure supporting Kiev’s war effort. The Defense Ministry in Moscow maintains that it never targets civilians.

articles.title: Iran's supreme leader warns US, Israel against new attacks
articles.body:
Breadcrumb
Iran's supreme leader warns US, Israel against new attacks
Iran's supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei on Saturday warned the United States and Israel against returning to war, according to a written statement, following threats from the Islamic republic's foes of a possible resumption of strikes.
"If the enemies once again launch military or terrorist attacks, it is the armed forces of the Islamic Republic and the Iranian nation that will determine the time and conditions for ending them," said a statement attributed to Khamenei posted on his website.
The remarks came during a reported meeting between Khamenei and senior military commanders, including armed forces chief of staff Ali Abdollahi, army chief Amir Hatami and Revolutionary Guards commander Ahmad Vahidi. It was the first reported meeting between them.
Khamenei has not been publicly seen since he became supreme leader, following his father Ayatollah Ali Khamenei's killing in US-Israeli strikes at the start of the Middle East war in February.
According to the statement, Khamenei ordered the commanders to ensure that "any level or type of threat must be met with an immediate, impactful and geographically unrestricted response".
It also said that Khamenei ordered the commanders to update Iran's target list to include "all types of tangible and intangible assets belonging to the American-Zionist enemy".
The war began on February 28 with US-Israeli strikes on Iran, which swiftly responded with attacks on countries around the region.
The supreme leader's statement came as fresh diplomatic efforts were under way to avert a resumption of fighting.
A Qatari delegation arrived in Tehran on Friday for talks with Iranian officials, after Iran reportedly received a letter from US Vice President JD Vance.
According to Iranian media, Tehran had yet to respond to the letter.

articles.title: Britain’s most powerful nuclear sub enters final build phase
articles.body:
The Dreadnought programme has entered a phase that will take the first boat through the completion of her build, sea trials and certification before she enters service in the early 2030s, while the second submarine progresses to sea trials of her own, according to an answer given in Parliament.
James MacCleary, the Liberal Democrat member for Lewes, asked what progress has been made on the Dreadnought programme in the context of the delivery confidence assessments for Government Major Project Portfolio defence projects.
Luke Pollard, Minister of State for Defence, said: “Good progress is being made on the Dreadnought programme. In July, we announced Delivery Phase 4 (DP4), the latest phase of the programme, which will enable the first-in-class submarine, Dreadnought, to complete her build, sea trials and certification, ahead of entering service in the early 2030s. During this phase, the second boat will progress to sea trials, while the third and fourth boats will achieve key construction milestones.”
Delivery Phase 4 is the funding and contracting step that carries the programme from construction into the trials and certification work needed before a ballistic missile submarine can take on operational patrols. Dreadnought, Valiant, Warspite and King George VI will replace the four Vanguard boats that have maintained continuous at sea deterrence since 1969, and the oldest of those, HMS Vanguard, commissioned in 1993 against a design life of twenty-five years.
Stretching the Vanguard class beyond that design life has produced the longest deterrent patrols in Royal Navy history, including a 204-day patrol completed by HMS Vanguard, and the Defence Committee has examined the strain that places on crews and on the maintenance cycle. The programme’s schedule matters for that reason as much as for the capability itself.
Construction runs at Barrow-in-Furness, where BAE Systems is expanding the yard to build Dreadnought and SSN-AUKUS alongside each other, and Rolls-Royce Submarines in Derby supplies the reactor cores. Major facility upgrades needed for Dreadnought core production have been delivered, with work now focused on commissioning and manufacture.
The Defence Investment Plan commits £63 billion over four years to the nuclear enterprise, taking in the submarines, a new sovereign warhead and the infrastructure at Barrow, Derby, Faslane, Coulport and Aldermaston.

articles.title: Zelensky: 500 Patriot interceptors could provide Ukraine with strong defense this winter
articles.body:
Zelensky: 500 Patriot interceptors could provide Ukraine with strong defense this winter
The President of Ukraine made the statement in a post on Telegram, Ukrinform reports.
“Five hundred PAC-3 interceptors is a substantial number, and very soon – this winter – they COULD make for a highly effective defense package. However, it has been stipulated that deliveries may begin ONLY IN A FEW YEARS. We are asking our American partners to find a solution for the time when there is a real danger and a real need to use PAC-3 interceptors,” he wrote.
Zelensky noted that Russia is striking Ukraine’s energy infrastructure every day. In the last two weeks of October alone, there have been more than 30 Russian strikes on critical parts of Ukraine’s energy grid. Now, on the eve of winter, Putin has begun carrying out his strike campaign against the essential services that sustain Ukrainian cities and communities. The targets are electricity, heating, water supply, bridges and life in the cities in general.
“We did ask our American partners to provide Ukraine with a winter support package – at a rate of 100 Patriot interceptors per month. Five hundred missiles would be enough to protect our skies over the coming months – precisely when it is so important for Ukraine to be in a strong position in negotiations and for Russia NOT to succeed in breaking life in Ukrainian cities and communities,” the head of state said.
He recalled that the United States, European countries and other partners around the world have sufficient stocks of PAC-3 interceptors: “Providing them to Ukraine right now – in the winter of 2026–2027 – and replenishing our partners’ arsenals LATER, in THE FOLLOWING YEARS, through this production already contracted and paid for by Ukraine and our partners would be the right approach. And it is entirely feasible.”
Zelensky expressed gratitude to President Trump, the State Department and the U.S. administration as a whole for the authorization.
“But we are asking for decisions that can guarantee the protection of lives not the day after tomorrow or sometime later, but at the very moment the threat is there – when Russia is killing and destroying. I thank everyone who stands with Ukraine!” the President concluded.
As Ukrinform reported, the U.S. State Department has approved a possible sale to Ukraine of 500 PAC-3 MSE missiles for Patriot air defense systems, worth a total of $2.1 billion.

articles.title: Iran's Khamenei warns US and Israel against new attacks
articles.body:
Iran's Khamenei warns US and Israel against new attacks
Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei warned the United States and Israel on Saturday against further strikes as fears mount over a resumption of fighting in the Middle East. US President Donald Trump and his Israeli ally Benjamin Netanyahu have recently threatened military action on the Islamic republic but US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Trump had not yet made a decision about fresh strikes.
Iran's supreme leader on Saturday warned the United States and Israel against launching new attacks following their threats to resume strikes after crucial elections, as fears mount over a return to fighting.
The declaration came as the Islamic republic's top diplomat said there were no plans to hold talks with the United States, as indirect mediation via Qatar continues.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Saturday Trump had not yet made a decision about fresh strikes.
"We can achieve military objectives if we seek to. He hasn't made a decision. I have no announcement in that regard with you today, and nor do we take any of it lightly," Rubio said at a G20 press conference in Atlanta, Georgia.
But Rubio added that Trump "hasn't made a decision" on further military action, amid reports that the US leader could attack after key midterm elections on Tuesday.
"I have no announcement in that regard with you today, and nor do we take any of it lightly," Rubio said.
While he slammed Tehran for "actively and openly" targeting commercial vessels for attack, Rubio also expressed Trump's preference for a diplomatic solution to end war with Iran.
But he did not commit to a timeline for talks.
Watch moreReports show US and Israel are planning new strikes on Iran
US President Donald Trump had previously warned of fresh military action after the US holds midterm elections early next week, saying last weekend that he was weighing whether to "finish them off".
In Israel, which is coming off fresh elections, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has spoken of a "historic, one-time opportunity" to topple the Iranian government.
Polls in both countries could determine the direction of the conflict, with Israel having voted Tuesday but yet to form a new government.
"Any level or type of threat must be met with an immediate, impactful and geographically unrestricted response," Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei told top military commanders in a meeting, according to a statement.
The encounter was the first reported meeting between Khamenei and military top brass, and included armed forces chief of staff Ali Abdollahi, army chief Amir Hatami and Revolutionary Guards commander Ahmad Vahidi.
The supreme leader has not been seen publicly since before he took the helm in March after the killing of his father Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in US-Israeli strikes.
Khamenei also ordered commanders to update Iran's target list to include "all types of tangible and intangible assets belonging to the American-Zionist enemy".
Iran has previously warned it would consider severing undersea cables in the Strait of Hormuz.
Petrol prices weigh on US vote
Since the initial US-Israeli strikes in February, ordinary Iranians "have been left in a state of limbo for the past year", Fariba, a Tehran housewife, told AFP.
But other residents in the Iranian capital brushed off the possible return to full-scale conflict.
"We do not fear another war. We have been at war for 48 years now," said Ebrahim, a salesman in his forties.
Since the outbreak of the war, Tehran has restricted shipping through the strategic waterway, which normally carries around one-fifth of global oil consumption.
Watch moreTrump vs MAGA: Why his movement is splitting
The blockade has caused a spike in global energy prices, making the war unpopular among the US public ahead of midterm congressional elections Tuesday.
Gains for the opposition Democrats could restrict, to an extent, Trump's ability to enact policy.
Voting in Israel has left Netanyahu's political camp with the most seats in parliament but short of a majority, leaving the make-up of the next administration unclear.
Read more'Atmosphere of fear': Trump moves to curtail voting rights ahead of the midterms
'Flames of war'
The war began on February 28 with US-Israeli strikes on Iran. The Islamic republic swiftly responded with attacks on American assets in countries around the region.
Fresh diplomatic efforts are underway to avert any resumption of fighting, with Qatari mediators landing in Tehran on Friday, and US Vice President JD Vance sending a letter to Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei.
But Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Saturday that "currently, there are no plans for meetings with American officials".
"Iran's conditions are clear, and consultations regarding them are ongoing among mediators," he said in an interview with Al Jazeera, according to the state news agency IRNA.
Read moreAre fresh US-Israeli strikes on Iran in the pipeline?
Qatar and Pakistan have been mediating between the warring parties, but the talks have yet to produce a lasting agreement.
The Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday that Vance had sent his letter to Iran's security chief at Trump's direction in a bid to revive negotiations and avert further US strikes.
Araghchi confirmed that Iran received the letter, saying, "The American side's effort to open a dialogue and reach a broader understanding is viewed as a positive step."
But the Iranian side kept firm its warnings against further attacks.
Earlier on Saturday, army spokesman Mohammad Akaraminia said that any resumption of hostilities would only expand the scope of the war.
"The flames of war will undoubtedly engulf a much wider geographical area," he said on social media, without elaborating.
Araghchi warned on X of an "Earth-shattering blow Iran's Powerful Armed Forces will deal against those who dare harm our people".
He said there would no longer be any "red lines".

articles.title: FLEX L12 “forest monster” makes autonomous debut with 5-ton load
articles.body:
- UGV Defence’s FLEX L12 drove a 1.7 km off-road course fully autonomously with 5 tons of cargo at Norway’s Camp Rødsmoen on Oct. 29.
- About 100 participants, mainly from the Norwegian and Swedish armed forces, saw the demo alongside partners including Kongsberg and BAE Systems.
Norwegian company UGV Defence has run its FLEX L12 heavy unmanned ground vehicle fully autonomously through a 1.7 km (1.1-mile) off-road course while carrying 5 metric tons (11,000 pounds) of cargo, in a demonstration for Nordic military officers at Camp Rødsmoen in Norway, Chief Executive Carl Ivarsson said on social media.
The tracked vehicle climbed steep inclines and drove through mud, water, large rocks, narrow passages and sharp turns without a driver, Ivarsson said. About 100 people attended the event on Oct. 29, mainly from the Norwegian and Swedish armed forces along with defense industry representatives.
UGV Defence used the day to present what it calls the Nordic Autonomous Mission Platform, a group of companies building equipment around the FLEX L12. The partners include Kongsberg, BAE Systems, Swedish sideloader maker Hammar, Safe-Tec, SKJOLDR and Nordic Shelter. Each company explained how the vehicle could support its products, and several showed their own systems at the event, though Ivarsson did not say which payloads were demonstrated on the vehicle.
“The feedback from defence and industry representatives was very encouraging. More importantly, the day demonstrated what can be achieved when leading Nordic defence companies bring together their expertise around a common autonomous platform,” said Ivarsson.
The FLEX L12 is far larger than most unmanned ground vehicles in service. Its L12-L cargo version is rated for up to 12 tons of payload, and a power-generation variant, the L12-P, carries up to 9 tons with a much larger battery. The vehicle uses a diesel-electric drive, has a top speed of 25 km/h (16 mph) and a stated range of up to 800 km (500 miles), the company said when it showed a civilian version at the DALO Industry Days exhibition in Denmark in August. By comparison, Ukraine’s Protector, one of the largest ground drones in Ukrainian service, weighs about 4 tons in total.
UGV Defence built the FLEX L12 on a civilian tracked carrier and has been reworking it for military use, with a military configuration being prepared for series production. The company has said on its website that deliveries of the FLEX L12-L cargo version are planned from the first quarter of 2027, and it has described possible uses including cargo transport, weapons integration and mobile power generation.
Rødsmoen, near Rena in eastern Norway, is a Norwegian Army camp, and the surrounding training area has hosted earlier unmanned vehicle trials, including a 10-day European Defence Agency test of armed ground robots in February.

articles.title: Iran warns fresh US strikes would unleash ‘flames of war’ far beyond current conflict
articles.body:
Fresh US strikes will unleash ‘geographically unrestricted response’, Iran’s supreme leader warns
- Iran warned that fresh US strikes would spread the war wider, with spokesman Mohammad Akraminia saying “the flames of war” could engulf a much larger area.
- Qatar and Pakistan are mediating, and a Qatari delegation met Iranian officials in Tehran as US Vice-President J.D. Vance sent a letter to reopen talks.
- The conflict has hit the Strait of Hormuz and global energy supplies, while US and Israeli elections may shape the next steps and risks of more fighting.
AI generated
TEHRAN – Iran’s supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei warned the United States and Israel on Oct 31 against returning to war, following threats from the Islamic republic’s foes of a possible resumption of strikes.
“If the enemies once again launch military or terrorist attacks, it is the armed forces of the Islamic Republic and the Iranian nation that will determine the time and conditions for ending them,” said a statement attributed to Khamenei that was posted on his website.
The remarks came during a reported meeting between Khamenei and senior military commanders, including armed forces chief of staff Ali Abdollahi, army chief Amir Hatami and Revolutionary Guards commander Ahmad Vahidi. It was the first reported meeting among them.
Khamenei has not been publicly seen since he became supreme leader, following his father Ayatollah Ali Khamenei’s killing in US-Israeli strikes at the start of the Middle East war in February.
According to the statement, Khamenei ordered the commanders to ensure that “any level or type of threat must be met with an immediate, impactful and geographically unrestricted response”.
It also said that Khamenei ordered the commanders to update Iran’s target list to include “all types of tangible and intangible assets belonging to the American-Zionist enemy”.
Khamenei’s threat was in line with a statement issued earlier in the day by Iran’s army warning that any new US attack would only spread the war wider.
The Iranian warning comes with fresh diplomatic efforts under way to avert a resumption of fighting, with Qatari mediators in Tehran and US Vice-President J.D. Vance reportedly sending a letter to Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei.
“If the US president once again embarks on more regional adventurism under pressure from, and in an attempt to appease, the Zionists, the flames of war will undoubtedly engulf a much wider geographical area,” Iranian army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia said in a post on X, without elaborating.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi also warned on Oct 31 that “Iran’s Powerful Armed Forces will deal against those who dare harm our people”.
On Oct 30, a Qatari delegation arrived in the Iranian capital for talks with senior Iranian officials.
Qatar and Pakistan have been mediating between the warring parties, but the talks have yet to produce a lasting agreement.
The Wall Street Journal reported on Oct 28 that Vance sent his letter to Iran’s security chief at the direction of President Donald Trump in a bid to revive negotiations and avert further US strikes.
Iran has confirmed receiving the letter but has not announced any response.
The US holds midterm elections on Nov 3 that could determine the direction of the war, which has proven unpopular with American voters following a spike in energy prices due to the conflict.
Israel also held legislative elections, with voters given a chance to offer a verdict on right-wing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
Under Netanyahu, who has vowed to topple Iran’s government, Israel and Iran have engaged in direct military confrontations after decades of shadow war.
The Middle East war began in late February with US-Israeli strikes on Iran that killed the country’s supreme leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, as well as senior military commanders.
Iran, in response, targeted US assets across the Middle East, as well as Israel.
Most recently, hostilities have focused on the Strait of Hormuz, a crucial Gulf shipping route for energy exports that Iran has blockaded since the start of the war.
The US has, in retaliation, been blockading Iranian ports in an attempt to squeeze Iran’s economy. AFP

articles.title: SSU detains suspect accused of guiding Russian strikes on defense plants and military units in Khmelnytskyi region
articles.body:
SSU detains suspect accused of guiding Russian strikes on defense plants and military units in Khmelnytskyi region
As reported by Ukrinform, the SSU said this in a statement.
According to the investigation, the man “guided combined enemy strikes on military units, defense plants and postal terminals.”
According to investigators, in preparation for the attacks, he “walked around the regional center and its outskirts, where, under the guise of making phone calls, he filmed the locations of potential ‘targets.’”
SSU officers detained the suspect while he was conducting additional reconnaissance near one of the strategically important facilities.
“It has been established that the agent carried out assignments from the FSB after being recruited as a local unemployed man who had previously been convicted of drug possession. He came to the attention of the Russian intelligence service while looking for work through Telegram channels. After being recruited, he tracked the locations of defense industry enterprises and the permanent deployment sites of Ukrainian troops. He then ‘switched’ to identifying the coordinates of logistics hubs and sorting terminals operated by postal companies. He stored the data he collected on his smartphone in the form of marked locations on electronic maps,” the SSU said.
According to the SSU, a mobile phone containing evidence of his work for Russia was found during searches of the suspect's premises.
SSU investigators served the man with a notice of suspicion under Part 2 of Article 111 of the Criminal Code of Ukraine (high treason committed under martial law).
The suspect is being held in custody. He faces life imprisonment with confiscation of property.
As reported by Ukrinform, a court sentenced two Russian agents exposed for carrying out an act of sabotage in Odesa in February last year to 15 years in prison with confiscation of property.

articles.title: Rubio says Iran talks have never stopped, stresses US preference for diplomacy
articles.body:
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Saturday that diplomatic contacts with Iran have continued despite escalating tensions in the Middle East, stressing that Washington remains open to a peaceful solution provided its core security concerns are addressed, Anadolu reports.
Speaking to reporters in Atlanta, Rubio said there was no set timetable for the ongoing diplomatic efforts, but emphasized that communication channels remained open.
“There are multiple talks. Talks have actually never stopped,” he said, adding that conversations were taking place both directly and, more often, through intermediaries.
“The president’s preference in any challenge around the world is to try to solve it diplomatically and peacefully, if possible,” Rubio said, referring to President Donald Trump’s approach.
He added that Washington would welcome a diplomatic outcome, provided it did not endanger US national security or leave its principal concerns unresolved.

At the center of those concerns, Rubio said, are Iran’s nuclear program and what Washington sees as Tehran’s destabilizing role across the region.
He accused Iran of targeting commercial shipping in international waters, warning that attacks on vessels carrying oil, natural gas and other cargo threaten not only maritime security but also global energy and food supplies.
Rubio also pointed to Iran’s support for regional groups, including the Houthis in Yemen and Hezbollah in Lebanon, arguing that their activities have contributed to instability and security concerns for neighboring countries.
Addressing Gulf security, he reaffirmed Washington’s defense commitments to Saudi Arabia, saying the US remained in regular contact with Riyadh and intended to honor its agreements.

Ukrainian arms manufacturer Fire Point claims to have overcome Starlink restrictions for long-range strikes – Reuters
Iryna Terekh, CEO of Ukrainian missile and drone manufacturer Fire Point, says the company has found a way of delivering long-range strikes in Russia and Russian-occupied territories without relying on Starlink satellite communications.
Source: Terekh in an interview with Reuters
Details: Terekh said the company has found workarounds that allow it to conduct strikes without using satellite communications.
Quote: "We have built with this in mind. Fire Point systems are designed to finish a mission without a satellite link. Navigation that works without any external signal is a priority."
Details: Terekh declined to disclose details of the solutions.
Quote: "We found a way to technologically overcome this challenge, but this only covers probably 15 to 20% of what we could do if the Starlink was working (over Russia)."

- On 22 October, the WSJ reported that US President Donald Trump had allegedly called Elon Musk and asked him to lift the restrictions on Starshield in Ukraine.

articles.title: Millions embezzled in fraud scheme at Ukrainian defense firm – investigators
articles.body:
Millions embezzled in fraud scheme at Ukrainian defense firm – investigators
A former head of a state-owned Ukrainian defense company is suspected of embezzling millions of dollars through fake mediation deals, the country’s anti-corruption bodies have said.
Ukraine’s National Anti-Corruption Bureau (NABU) and Specialized Anti-Corruption Prosecutor’s Office (SAPO) announced in a statement on Friday that the scheme had cost the government 1.1 billion hryvnia (around $43 million).
The Western-backed agencies, which frequently target Ukrainian leader Vladimir Zelensky’s inner-circle, didn’t name the suspect, only saying that he used to lead a subsidiary of Ukrspecexport, a state-run company with exclusive rights to export and import military hardware.
According to the investigators, the former head of the state-run firm signed a deal with a foreign company in 2015 for it to provide mediation during the sales of Ukrainian military products abroad.
However, it had been established that the Ukrainian firm had conducted all of the negotiations with a customer from a Middle Eastern country on its own, and the foreign company wasn’t involved, they said.
Despite this fact, the official signed falsified documents about mediation services being provided by the foreign company and transferred millions to it as payment, the statement read.
The actions of the suspect are being qualified as large-scale embezzlement and forgery of government papers, it added.
Ukrainskaya Pravda reported later in the day that, according to its sources, the official in question is Taras Shiyko, who now holds the positions of the deputy director of Ukroboronprom, a state-run conglomerate comprised of Ukraine’s arms makers. The fraud scheme relates to his time as the head of Progress, a state-run export and import company.
Shiyko became part of an anti-corruption case earlier this year, involving the suspected embezzlement of 32 million hryvnia (around $700,000).
Zelensky’s government has been rocked by a series of corruption scandals involving people close to him since November 2025, when NABU and SAPO accused Timur Mindich, a longtime associate of the Ukrainian leader, of masterminding a $100 million kickback scheme involving state contracts in the energy sector. Other investigations have implicated former Ukrainian ministers, diplomats, and senior officials.
NABU’s latest high-profile case targeted an alleged protection racket involving scam call centers and officials from the Prosecutor General’s Office. Although he was not personally named as a suspect, Prosecutor General Ruslan Kravchenko left Ukraine before being dismissed by parliament last month, according to Ukrainian media.
Critics accuse Zelensky of leading a sprawling corruption network which permeates his government, allegedly helping him maintain power and enriching those involved. A poll issued by the Kiev International Institute of Sociology (KIIS) last month suggested that the Ukrainians consider corruption to be a bigger problem for the country than the conflict with Russia.

articles.title: Iran reports destruction of US drone and three tanker incidents in Strait of Hormuz
articles.body:
Iran reports destruction of US drone and three tanker incidents in Strait of Hormuz
TEHRAN – Iran’s armed forces have reported the destruction of two different American unmanned platforms and incidents involving three oil tankers attempting to navigate unauthorized routes through the Strait of Hormuz, as the country maintains restrictions on maritime traffic through the strategic waterway.
In separate announcements on Thursday and Friday, the Islamic Revolution Guards Corps (IRGC) Navy and the Iranian Army Navy reported the interception of an American MQ-1 unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV), the destruction of an enemy unmanned surface vessel (USV), and incidents involving three oil tankers accused of disregarding Iranian navigation regulations and safety warnings.
The announcements underscore Iran’s continued emphasis on enforcing its maritime security arrangements in the Strait of Hormuz and preventing unauthorized movements through designated shipping routes.
Three oil tankers involved in incidents
In a statement issued on Friday, the IRGC Navy announced that two oil tankers attempting to pass through unauthorized routes in the eastern and western sections of the Strait of Hormuz had encountered incidents and were stopped in the southern waters of the strategic waterway.
According to the statement, both vessels had switched off their navigation and positioning systems and attempted to leave the strait through unauthorized routes with the support of the US military.
The IRGC Navy said the tankers had ignored repeated radio warnings, entered areas designated as unsafe, and subsequently encountered incidents before being halted.
The force attributed the incidents and fires aboard the vessels to 'hostile actions by the US military,' as well as the tankers’ disregard for Iranian regulations governing navigation through the strait.
In a separate announcement, the IRGC Navy reported that a supertanker had exploded after striking a naval mine while attempting to navigate an unauthorized route through the waterway.
The vessel, which was carrying more than two million barrels of oil, was left burning near the entrance to the Strait of Hormuz, according to the statement.
The IRGC Navy described the supertanker as the third oil tanker to have suffered an explosion and caught fire on Friday after attempting to use unauthorized routes.
The announcements did not identify the vessels or disclose their flags, ownership, or the precise circumstances of the incident.
Iranian Navy destroys unmanned surface vessel
Separately, the Iranian Army Navy announced that its forces had destroyed an enemy unmanned surface vessel operating in the eastern Strait of Hormuz in the early hours of Friday.
According to the Navy's public relations office, the remotely operated vessel was struck and destroyed while moving and conducting operations within the area monitored by Iranian naval forces.
The Navy also reported that two enemy oil tankers had sustained damage and caught fire after striking naval mines while navigating restricted and unsafe waters east of the Strait of Hormuz with their tracking systems switched off.
It said the vessels had disregarded previously issued warnings and maritime regulations, adding that their owners would bear full responsibility for the consequences of unauthorized navigation and failure to observe safety instructions.
The Navy warned that any hostile movement, infiltration or provocative action in areas monitored by Iran's armed forces would be met with a firm and proportionate response.
IRGC downs American MQ-1 drone
In a separate development announced on Thursday, the IRGC reported that its Aerospace Division had intercepted and destroyed an American MQ-1 unmanned aerial vehicle over the eastern Strait of Hormuz.
According to a statement published on the IRGC's official website, the drone was brought down by an advanced air defense system operating within Iran's integrated air defense network.
 
The IRGC described the aircraft as the 14th advanced MQ-1 drone intercepted and destroyed.
The aerial drone incident is distinct from the Iranian Army Navy's announcement concerning the destruction of an unmanned surface vessel. The two statements refer to different platforms and separate military operations.
Iran emphasizes control over maritime traffic
Iran has repeatedly warned commercial vessels against using navigation routes that have not been authorized by its maritime authorities, emphasizing that compliance with designated corridors and safety instructions is essential to preventing incidents in the Strait of Hormuz.
Since the US-Israeli war of aggression against Iran began on February 28, 2026, Tehran has introduced new arrangements governing maritime traffic through the strait, citing security considerations and the need to protect its territorial waters and national interests.
The Strait of Hormuz, connecting the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and the wider Indian Ocean, is one of the world's most strategically important maritime passages. A substantial share of internationally traded crude oil and petroleum products passes through this waterway, making maritime security and uninterrupted commercial navigation there a matter of international economic importance.
Iran maintains that safe passage through the strait requires vessels to observe the regulations established by the coastal authorities and refrain from unauthorized movements, particularly amid heightened regional tensions.
The latest announcements by the IRGC Navy and the Iranian Army Navy reinforce Tehran's warning that vessels operating in the area must comply with its maritime security instructions and that unauthorized navigation in designated restricted zones carries serious risks.
